name: Deutschlandstipendium (Germany Scholarship)

universities: Participating public and state-recognised universities across Germany (apply directly to your own university; e.g. TU München, RWTH Aachen, LMU, etc.)

duration: At least 2 semesters, up to the standard period of study
eligibleNationalities: Open to all nationalities (nationality is not material to the award). Bangladeshi nationals enrolled at — or admitted to — a participating German university may apply. Doctoral candidates and students at federal universities (Hochschulen des Bundes) are excluded.
languageRequirements: No central language test; set by the host university for admission. At TUM, application documents may be submitted in German or English.
minGPA: Set by each university; at TUM, minimum German grade of 2.40 for university entrance qualification / enrolled students.
fundingCovers: 300 EUR/month cash support (150 EUR private sponsor + 150 EUR Federal Government match)
Non-material support at many universities: mentoring, networking events, internships
renewalConditions: Reviewed every two semesters; the university checks whether the holder still meets the award/minimum-grade criteria and whether private sponsor funding remains available.
intake: Winter semester 2026/2027 (October 2026 start of funding year)
requiredDocuments: Online application via the host university's portal (apply directly to your own German university)
Cover letter / letter of motivation (max ~1.5 pages, German or English) explaining why you should receive the scholarship
Tabular CV (1-2 pages, German or English, chronological)

Proof of academic performance (Bachelor: university entrance qualification grade / uni-assist grade; Master: Bachelor's grade or current transcript of records / uni-assist grade if degree not from EU/EEA/Switzerland)

Optional supporting evidence for 'soft factors' (volunteering/commitment confirmations, employment contracts, prizes/awards, and proof of special circumstances such as illness, childcare, care of a relative, orphanhood, refugee status, or migration background)
All documents in German or English, uploaded as PDFs
On acceptance: proof of German residence, German bank account and tax ID (Steuer-ID)

timeline.opens: Set per university; at TUM, application windows in May and July 2026
timeline.deadline: Set by each participating university (no central deadline). Example — TUM 2026/2027: enrolled students / pre-2026 entrance qualification May 18-31, 2026 (expired); 2026 high-school graduates July 13-26, 2026
timeline.resultsBy: At TUM, selection committee meets in September; admission offers sent from October; first payment by mid-December at the latest
timeline.notes: Anchored to 2026-06: there is no single national deadline — each participating university sets its own application window and documents; you apply directly to the German university where you are enrolled or admitted. Dates shown are the TUM 2026/2027 funding-year cycle (verified 2026-06-18); other universities differ. Funding year runs 1 October to 30 September.

benefits: 300 EUR per month (150 EUR from a private sponsor + 150 EUR matched by the German Federal Government)
Paid irrespective of personal or parental income; can be combined with BAföG (does not count towards BAföG funding)
Frequently includes non-material support: mentoring, networking events, internships, contact with industry sponsors
Awarded for at least two semesters, up to the standard period of study
mustKnow: PARTIAL award, not full funding: a flat 300 EUR/month only — it does NOT pay tuition and is not a full living stipend. The wiki lists it for completeness.
You must already be enrolled at, or admitted to, a participating German university — this is NOT a route to come to Germany. You apply directly to your own university, not to a central body.
Doctoral candidates and students at federal universities (Hochschulen des Bundes) cannot apply.
On accepting an offer you must be a German resident with a German bank account (and provide a tax ID); without these the offer lapses — secure a visa/residence early.
No central deadline or document list: each university sets its own application window and required documents (the document/deadline details here are TUM's example).
Selection weighs academic record plus 'soft factors' (social commitment, personal circumstances); committees may invite applicants to interviews.
You may not hold another talent/performance-based award averaging 30 EUR/month or more at the same time; cannot be combined with doctoral funding. BAföG is allowed alongside it.
Funding is reviewed every two semesters and continues only if you still meet the criteria and private sponsor funding remains available.
